column1: # Trials whose apparatus failure could not be fixed, and which are therefore
# published as excluded rows instead of being re-run (#347).
# docs/unknown-rate.md states the rule this file serves: "SETUP_ERROR is an
# apparatus failure, not a refusal: fix the apparatus and re-run that trial; if
# unfixable, the row is published as excluded, with the reason." The first half is
# the default and needs no record. This file is the second half: count.py refuses
# a generation marked complete that carries a SETUP_ERROR not listed here, so the
# judgement "this one could not be fixed" is made once, in a commit, in front of a
# reviewer — rather than by a sweep that drops the row and publishes the rate from
# what remains. The report's own message says what failed; it cannot say whether
# Every row here must also BE a SETUP_ERROR in some complete generation. A waiver
# that outlives the trial it excused would sit here excusing nothing.
# The reason is published verbatim in the per-trial table, so it carries no pipe
# (the markdown row would split) and is written to be read, never matched. A
# newline cannot reach the table: read_ledger splits the file into lines, so the
# cell is always one line. What a stray newline costs is the rest of the reason,
# dropped in silence — the diff shows it as two rows.
